# Librarian log

Append-only. Entries are grouped under a `## YYYY-MM-DD` heading, and **each entry is one line
beginning with its kind**, so the log stays greppable:

```
- ingest: <what was read; what was created, updated, deprecated, and why>
- miss: <what the brief or an answer failed to supply, and where it surfaced>
- measure: brief=<bytes>
- lint: <findings>
- process: <a finding about the ritual or the harness itself, rather than about the corpus>
- harness: <a change to the files that instruct an agent, DECIDED in the session, as a work item>
```

`harness:` was **agreed by the owner on 2026-08-19** and reached this file at the ingest of
2026-08-20, having stood in `.superpowers/sdd/vault-feedback.md` alone in the interval. It is a
change to the files that instruct an agent — a skill, a hook, `CLAUDE.md`, a template, the check —
**decided** rather than observed, which is what separates it from `process:`: that one is a
*finding* about the ritual, this one is a *work item* already taken
([[harness-is-a-feedback-kind-of-its-own]], [[a-harness-change-is-recorded-when-it-is-decided]]).
The handoff's `Harness` section is a work queue and its lines arrive here under this kind rather
than being translated into another.
*(The vocabulary lives in two files and this is the librarian's copy. The word was added to both by
hand, which is the copy this store has already flagged; the durable fix — a `wiki/rules/` page with
a region in each file — is designed nowhere
([[the-drain-and-the-template-disagree-about-the-feedback-vocabulary]],
[[no-rule-reads-a-harness-file]]).)*

`process:` was **agreed by the owner on 2026-08-17**, after two entries had already been filed
under it, and the wording above matches the copy in `.superpowers/sdd/vault-feedback.md`. Neither
of those two entries was a `miss:` — the vault supplied what it had — nor a `lint:`, which is a
judgement about pages, nor a `measure:`, which carries a number. The kind was not carelessness: the
other three genuinely did not cover it ([[process-is-a-feedback-kind-for-the-ritual-not-the-corpus]]).

A finding is reported by a session through the `Feedback to the librarian` section of its handoff
and transferred here by `/ingest`, **under the kind the line already names**. A working agent never
writes to this file directly — the vault has one writer, and the scope of that rule now includes
this file and the other registers ([[the-one-writer-rule-covers-the-registers-too]]).
*(The paragraph above said "section 7 of its handoff" until 2026-08-17; the journal's sections lost
their numbers and the cut is by heading text.)*

  template, which is what a limitation of this kind waits for.
  *(An earlier version of this entry said prose was uncounted and a prose document would have a
  denominator near zero. That was wrong on both halves and is corrected here: paragraph openers
  are counted, and the no-blank-lines shape is handled in the script by name.)*

- lint: **`vault-coverage.sh` excludes headings from its denominator and says so nowhere.** Line 127
  is a bare `[ "$kind" = "heading" ] && continue`, with no comment, in a file where every other rule
  explains why it exists. The visible effect: `vault-units.sh` reports 93 units for the 2026-08-17
  journal while coverage reports `83 of 83`, and the two numbers look exactly like a check passing
  against a denominator smaller than the list it claims to check — this project's signature failure.
  **The review of that ingest reached for that conclusion and had to be talked out of it by reading
  the script**, which is the fourth claim that session nearly asserted without checking. The
  arithmetic is right and deliberate: the journal carries ten headings, and a heading is not a claim.
  One sentence beside the line would end it. **The same off-by-ten recurs on this ingest** — 91 unit
  lines against `81 of 81` from coverage, which is the ten headings again. Recorded a second time
  rather than fixed:
  the line is in a script, and `vault-scripts` already states the exclusion in prose.

- process: **file content must never travel inside a shell command string, and this cost two failures
  in one session.** Diagnosed rather than guessed: eight heredoc constructs were written to files and
  parsed — apostrophes, backticks, em dashes, arrows, HTML comments, backslashes, 200-line bodies — and
  **all eight parse cleanly**, so heredoc syntax is not the fault. The fault is the transport: the
  command reaches bash wrapped in quotes, and prose carrying backticks or apostrophes is then either
  executed as command substitution or breaks the wrapping. It fired once on the retro file and once,
  seconds later, in the very command written to investigate it — a code span in prose executed as a
  command, reported as *span: command not found*. The remedy is not a script, because the script is
  invoked by the same command: **prose is written with the file-writing tool, and a generator reads its
  input from a file rather than from an argument.** This is a rule-page candidate by the admission
  test, and it has a sibling already on the record:
  [[an-apostrophe-in-an-awk-comment-ends-the-shell-quote]].
  **It fired a third time during this ingest**, on the heredoc carrying this very log entry, and was
  answered the way the entry prescribes: written to a file and appended.

  uses and ran 1660 seconds — about 28 minutes.** Recorded through this channel because it is the
  only one it can arrive by: a subagent cannot see its own usage, the harness reports it to the main

  ([[a-subagent-cannot-report-its-own-cost]]). **What the number is:** one dispatch, one source, a
  534-line journal of 62 units, producing 22 pages created, 17 updated, 1 retired, four registers
  touched and the brief regenerated. **What it is not:** a rate, a cost per page, or a figure to
  convert — the round trip is a fixed cost per dispatch rather than per source, which is why
  `/ingest` batches dispatch while compiling one source at a time
  ([[agent-round-trip-cost]], [[an-unsourced-number-is-dropped-not-chosen]]). **The comparison worth
  keeping** is against the skill's own estimate of *15–30 minutes*: this one landed at the top of it,

  Prototyped 2026-08-19 at `6bb9a12` over the bodies of `wiki/`. **Naively 299 resolve and 168 do
  not, across 81 pages**; after two mechanical exclusions and one correction **the residual is 65

  `wiki/` body is written from the vault root, not the repository root (97 resolve on the second
  base, which is a base and not a heuristic)**. What the residual is, read: roughly 24 illustrations
  and placeholders, 8 web routes, 11 module paths written short, 6 paths deleted that session, and a
  handful genuinely dead. **So a detector is an advisory and can never be red**, because a page
  recording history is supposed to name a path that no longer exists
  ([[a-path-detector-for-prose-references]], [[fidelity-to-a-source-and-fidelity-to-the-tree]]).
- measure: **the gate's selftest is fully green for the first time**: `caught 124, missed 0` after

- measure: **correction to the session's own claim: the two schema loaders were not demonstrably
  broken, and the reason is that no carriage return reaches `awk` on this host.** GNU Awk 5.4.0
  under this shell, fed bytes `  - title\r\n`, reports `length($0) == 9`, and the unpatched loader
  printed `title` with no trailing CR — **this gawk reads in text mode and translates CRLF to LF
  before any rule sees a line**. So every `sub(/\r$/, "")` in `vault-check.sh` is inert here,
  including the one the page pass carries with a comment explaining why it is needed. **Where it is
  not inert is the container**, which is the same asymmetry `.gitattributes` already pins `*.sh`
  for. **What this corrects**: the earlier claim that the `*.yaml` pin made the loaders unreachable
  was wrong in both directions — they were unreachable *on this host* for a different reason, and
  never unreachable in the container. The pin and the fix are both still right
  ([[no-cr-reaches-awk-on-this-host-and-the-container-is-where-it-bites]]).

  codepoint range. **The wrong instrument agreed with itself across two separate runs**, which is how

## 2026-08-23 — `decided_by:` is back-filled across `wiki/rules/`, and one rule turns out to have no decision

**Fourteen of the fifteen rule pages gained `decided_by:`; one is left without it and reported to
the owner by name.** Nothing else was touched: no `_schema.yaml`, no `sources:` entry removed, no
page retired, no contradiction resolved. The field was inserted immediately after `sources:` on
every page, so the two provenance-shaped fields sit together and a reader meets the cause where he
already looks for the citations.

**The measurement given to this run was verified against the tree rather than believed, and it
holds exactly.** Resolving every `[[wikilink]]` in each rule's `sources:` against a `type:` sweep of
all 576 pages under `wiki/` and `archive/`: ten rules name at least one page whose `type:` is
`decision`, five name none, and the five are exactly the ones named —
`a-block-attributed-to-the-owner-is-written-in-his-own-russian`,
`a-pre-task-runs-between-the-plan-and-its-approval`,
`dispatch-librarians-in-parallel-only-for-reading`,
`no-new-entity-where-an-existing-one-can-carry-the-claim`,
`the-shared-reading-discipline-renders-into-every-agent-that-reads-the-vault`. Two of the ten reach
a decision only through `archive/`, and both reach the same one:
[[claude-md-is-a-map-and-four-rules]].

### What the field was read as, and why that reading is the corpus's own

**`sources:` is where a rule's decisions sit today, and it was the first place looked and never the
only one.** Four of the fifteen state their own cause in prose in the idiom this store already
writes — *"the decision behind it is X; this page carries the text that decision obliges"* — and
those four were taken from the page's own words:
[[no-new-entity-where-an-existing-one-can-carry-the-claim]],
[[a-block-attributed-to-the-owner-is-written-in-his-own-russian]],
[[a-pre-task-runs-between-the-plan-and-its-approval]] and
[[write-the-miss-into-vault-feedback-before-the-turn-ends]]. **That idiom fixed the reading for the
rest**: the cause is the ruling that decided the rule's *substance*, not the ruling that created the
folder, licensed the shape, or scheduled the migration. So no page took
[[rules-becomes-a-type-of-its-own]], which created `wiki/rules/` and would have been the same answer
fifteen times, and none took [[a-definition-may-render-into-the-repository-claude-md]] or
[[governs-becomes-a-property-of-any-page]], which licensed a shape rather than commanding a record.

### The one that has no decision, and it is a finding rather than a gap in this run

**[[ask-before-weakening-or-working-around-a-rule]] carries no `decided_by:`.** Its own `sources:`
name [[hand-edits-of-the-wiki-are-a-recorded-divergence]] (`authority: wiki-write-exception`) and
[[the-turn-that-explains-a-rule-adds-exceptions-to-it]] (a `lesson`) — **both are evidence the rule
cites for its second sentence, and neither is a ruling that the first sentence should exist.**
`bash scripts/vault-authority.sh --near ask-before-weakening-or-working-around-a-rule` returns no
group and three word-overlap families, none of which holds a decision about asking before a rule is
changed. A grep of `wiki/decisions/` for *ask before*, *work around* and *weaken* returns five pages,
every one about something else; the nearest is [[narrowing-a-scope-notifies-and-widening-it-asks]],
which is about an approved **scope** and not a rule.

**Traced to its origin instead of guessed at.** `git log -S "Ask before you weaken" -- CLAUDE.md`
returns exactly one commit, `36e9e4c` of 2026-08-14 — the same commit as the cut that
[[claude-md-is-a-map-and-four-rules]] records. **That decision does not account for the paragraph**:
its *test that chose the four* table does not contain it, and its *What the file is now* enumerates
the description, the language rule, the commands, the four rules, the map, the loop and the feedback
line — and not this. The journal of that day,
`raw/handoffs/2026-08-14-acceptance-and-the-shortened-claude-md.md`, does not mention weakening a
rule at all. **So the paragraph was written into the file by the session that shortened it, and no
ruling behind it was ever recorded** — which is a real hole, and it is worth more than a field
pointed at the nearest page. Left empty, and raised with the owner.

**It is not a small rule to be missing one.** It is the rule this corpus reaches for whenever two
rules collide: [[rules-becomes-a-type-of-its-own]],
[[the-suite-never-runs-against-the-production-database]],
[[an-ast-boundary-test-is-fixed-at-its-cause-not-in-the-test]] and
[[our-javascript-does-not-choose-which-rows-are-on-screen]] all cite it in the same
`RESOLVED BY THE OWNER` note, and [[every-rule-in-wiki-rules-owes-a-mechanical-instrument]] names it
as one of five rules nothing observes. **The obvious repair is not the librarian's**: writing a
`decisions/` page for a rule the owner never ruled on would be minting his decision for him.

- **Nothing left `sources:`.** A decision that is both cited and causal is now written twice, once in

  ([[an-exit-code-read-through-a-pipe-belongs-to-the-last-stage]]): `bash scripts/vault-inject.sh`,

## 2026-08-23 — the missing decision behind the ask-before-weakening rule is written, and the last `decided_by:` is filled

**The hole reported by the previous run is closed by an owner ruling and not by a link to the
nearest page.** [[ask-before-weakening-or-working-around-a-rule]] had no decision behind it: its
text entered `CLAUDE.md` at `36e9e4c` on 2026-08-14, written by the session that shortened the
file, and no ruling behind it was ever recorded. **The rule's text was read to the owner verbatim
at the retro of 2026-08-23**, he was told it had never been ruled and that the same shape had
already been struck once here, both directions were offered, and he ratified it —
«да, это мое решение. Подписываюсь». That is a real decision with a real date, and it is now a
page.

**Minted: [[the-ask-before-weakening-rule-is-ratified-after-being-enforced-without-a-decision]]**,
`authority: ask-before-weakening-ratification`, `binding: prohibition`, `basis: human`,
`decided: 2026-08-23`, `sprint: S3`. His Russian is at the head of the page, verbatim and
untidied, in a block attributed to him
([[a-block-attributed-to-the-owner-is-written-in-his-own-russian]]).

### What the lookup returned, and why a new page was still right

**`bash scripts/vault-authority.sh --near ask-before-weakening-ratification` returned no group** and
three word-overlap families, best first: *what the owner said, and what was put in his mouth* (2
shared words), *line endings* (1), *how the owner is asked* (1) and *a number this project quotes*
(1). **`--near ask-before-weakening-or-working-around-a-rule` was run as well** and also returned no
group, its word-overlap families being *a rule page and the slice that travels* and *what actually
reaches a subagent* — neither of which holds a question about whether a rule is the owner's.

**The nearest family is the right one and none of its members could carry the claim.**
`retro-ratification` is the procedure that ratifies a line, `retro-menu-attribution` is how a
choice from a menu is written down, `paraphrase-attribution-chain` is the failure class, and
`ratification-sweep-schedule` is the *schedule* of the sweep — it even sends the unratified
prohibition to the top of the list, which is a page about ordering the work and not about what the
owner then said. **The two pages that record an actual ratification each have one of their own**:
[[a-refusal-is-conditional-or-absolute-and-nothing-else]] carries its owner block on the page it
ratifies, because that page was already the decision. **Here there was no page to carry it** — the
whole finding is that the rule had no decision page at all — so the ratification had nowhere to be
appended and a `decisions/` page is what it is. `ask-before-weakening-ratification` joined the
family in `authority.md`, with the Russian and English aliases a future question would arrive in;
`bash scripts/vault-authority.sh --check` reports the register and the tree agreeing at 529 slugs.

### What the page carries, because two of the four are the point

- **the rule's text**, as what was ratified, quoted from `CLAUDE.md` and the rule page's slice;
- **that it predates its decision by nine days and was enforced throughout** — a retroactive
  ratification, written as one. The pages citing the rule are read from a `rg -l` rather than
  counted on the page, and four of them cite it inside the same `RESOLVED BY THE OWNER` note.
  Writing it as though the rule followed the ruling would falsify the record;
- **how the hole was found** — by a mechanical pass filling `decided_by:` across `wiki/rules/`,
  which had nowhere to point, and not by anyone doubting the rule while reading it. A required link
  is an audit that runs itself: it asks a page to *name* its foundation, and a page that cannot is
  visible in a way careful reading does not make it. That is the reusable half;
- **what it was chosen against** — striking it as never-ruled, which was genuinely on offer and is
  what happened to `advisory-is-the-default-for-a-hook`. The two cases have the same shape and
  different answers, which is the argument for asking rather than deciding.

**A short dated section was appended to the rule page itself**, so a reader who lands on the rule
rather than on the decision learns that it was ratified retroactively. It sits outside the
`<!-- text -->` slice, so nothing travels differently: the injector rewrote 0 regions.

### What this run does not do

- **`decided_by:` stays `optional:` in `wiki/rules/_schema.yaml`.** Promoting it is the session's
  and was explicitly reserved. Nothing in that file was touched.
- **The citation to this session's journal is owed and deliberately not written.** The document in
  which he was shown the text and answered does not exist yet — it is written at `/handoff` and
  compiled at `/ingest` — and a `sources:` path to a file that is not there reads as provenance and
  is not. The page says so, and says which ingest owes it. Same shape as
  [[a-refusal-is-conditional-or-absolute-and-nothing-else]], whose owed citation was written at the
  ingest that followed it.
- **Nothing was struck, retired or resolved.** The rule's text is unchanged to the byte, and
  [[every-rule-in-wiki-rules-owes-a-mechanical-instrument]] still names this rule as owing an
  instrument — a ratification settles whose rule it is, not whether anything can see it break.

  ([[an-exit-code-read-through-a-pipe-belongs-to-the-last-stage]]): `bash scripts/vault-inject.sh`,

## 2026-08-23 — the style rule lands, and its text is recovered from outside the repository

**The five lines were never lost.** The brief of today reports that `grep -ril KISS` over the whole
repository matches a journal and nothing else, that *the five lines survive only in the chat log*,
and that recovering them means asking the owner again. **The search was scoped to the repository,
and the text was never in the repository**: it is in the plan he approved when S3 was opened, at
`C:\Users\kir\.claude\plans\agile-percolating-wall.md`, lines 167 to 172, under phase A1 — outside
the tree by the language rule that puts it there
([[the-plan-the-owner-reads-to-approve-it-is-written-in-russian]]). The five lines travelled from
that file into the rule's slice **verbatim**, and the copy was diffed against the plan rather than
read against it: the diff is empty.

**Minted, in the order the schema forces.**

- **[[the-style-rule-is-ratified-and-its-text-recovered-from-the-approved-plan]]**,
  `authority: style-rule-ratification`, `binding: prohibition`, `basis: human`,
  `decided: 2026-08-23`, `sprint: S3`. First, because `wiki/rules/_schema.yaml` requires
  `decided_by:` and a rule with no decision to point at cannot be written at all.
- **[[write-plainly-name-the-source-and-say-what-is-not-done]]**, `governs: CLAUDE.md`,
  `render: region`, `basis: human`, `decided_by:` the page above, and no `authority:` — forbidden in
  that folder.

**No `owner:` block was written, and that is a finding rather than an omission.** Every journal in
`raw/handoffs/` and in `archive/*/*/handoffs/` was searched for his words on this rule. What exists
is `owner selected: мой вариант` in the journal of this morning's session — a **menu selection**,
carried as an option label, which the store's own rule says is neither a quotation nor a paraphrase
and is never signed `owner:`
([[the-retro-records-a-ruling-chosen-from-a-menu-and-ratifies-decisions-not-utterances]]). The
second ratification is an approval of a plan, which is a decision written in the session's voice
and signed by nobody — the same shape `sprint.md` states for S3's own goal and criteria. **Nothing
was invented to fill the gap**, and the decision page says so where a reader will meet it.

### What the lookup returned, and why a new page was still right

**`bash scripts/vault-authority.sh --near session-writing-style`**, run before the slug was minted,
returned one group with one member: *the prose this project writes* — `session-writing-style`, held
by [[a-style-rule-for-the-prose-a-session-writes]], with the script's own warning that *that
question has a page, do not write a second*.

**That page could not carry either claim, and the reason is the folder set rather than a
preference.** It is a `proposal`, and a proposal is by this store's definition never a record of
something that exists; it also cannot carry the rule's **text**, because only a page with `governs:`
is opened by the injector, and a `<!-- text -->` slice on a page with no `governs:` is red. So the
text needs a `wiki/rules/` page, and the ratification needs a `decisions/` page with a date and a
rejected alternative — neither of which is a thing a proposal is.

**The family gained a second slug rather than a second answer to the same question.**
`session-writing-style` asks *how should this be written*; `style-rule-ratification` asks *what was
ratified, and where its text came from*. `authority.md` carries both, with the recovery vocabulary
added as aliases — `где текст`, `план вне репозитория`, `восстановить текст` — because those are
the words the next question about this will arrive in, and none of them reached anything today.

### What was chosen against

**Asking the owner for the five lines a third time**, which the brief recommended. It would have
re-derived text that already existed and produced a third wording for a third ratification. The
ratified text is a document, not a topic.

**Copying the five lines onto the decision page as well.** Refused: the injector compares the rule's
slice against the region byte for byte, and prose on a decision page is compared against nothing.
This corpus has already paid for that — [[english-is-the-rule-and-the-russian-past-is-deferred]]
restates the language rule's list and had to be corrected on its own when a word was struck from the
slice.

**Putting the plan's path in `sources:`.** Refused: rule 2 of the gate tests every non-wikilink
entry of that field for existence and reddens on a path that resolves to nothing. The file is
outside version control, so the citation would rot into a red gate whose only repair is deleting the
one citation the page exists to make. It is in the body of both new pages instead, with its line
numbers.

- process: **[[a-style-rule-for-the-prose-a-session-writes]] was marked `status: implemented` and a
  dated section was appended to it.** Nothing on it was deleted: the section asserting the text
  survives only in the chat log is kept whole, and the appended section says which half of it was
  false and which half stands. Its title lost the clause *ratified and still unwritten*, corrected
  in place — a title correction moves no address and is not a supersession — and **the filename was
  not touched**.
- process: **the page has not moved to `archive/`, deliberately.** Both live pages name it, so the
  precondition `scripts/vault-archive.sh` enforces is satisfied; `archive/` is organised as one
  folder per session and this session's folder does not exist yet, so archiving now would file it
  under the previous session's name. The mark opens a state, and the move is the next session's.
- process: **the region was marked in the repository's `CLAUDE.md` by this dispatch**, under a new
  heading `## How to write it`, placed after `## Language` — which language to write in, then how to
  write it. Marking a region in a destination is normally the session's and not the librarian's; it
  was done here because the run was ordered end to end, and the diff is what the owner reads.
- process: **every `[[wikilink]]` written today was resolved against the tree before the file was
  saved**, by listing each slug and asking `find` for the file. Nothing was cited from memory.
- process: **two open questions were named and neither was answered**: whether the rule governs
  `wiki/` as well as `CLAUDE.md`, which was never put to him, and whether any instrument can check
  it — the rule owes one under acceptance criterion 1 of S3
  ([[every-rule-in-wiki-rules-owes-a-mechanical-instrument]]), and prose style is a judgement no
  linter here reads.
- process: **the readings that close this write, each exit code read from its own invocation**
  ([[an-exit-code-read-through-a-pipe-belongs-to-the-last-stage]]): `bash scripts/vault-inject.sh`,
  exit **0**, reporting one region rewritten, nothing generated, nothing removed and no problems;
  `bash scripts/vault-check.sh`, exit **0**, with the one pre-existing advisory about harness
  coverage and no new line; `bash scripts/vault-authority.sh --check`, exit **0**, the register and
  the tree agreeing at 530 slugs. The first `vault-check.sh` run was red —
  `'style-rule-ratification' is carried by a page and is in no group` — which is the register
  catching an unregistered slug exactly as it should; `authority.md` was filled and the rerun is the
  exit 0 above. No script changed here, so no selftest was run.

## 2026-08-24 — `decided_by:` is back-filled across `wiki/proposals/`, and six pages are left empty on purpose

**Twenty-six of the thirty-three proposals without the field gained one; one gained `status: idea`;
six were left with neither.** Nothing else moved: no body text, no other frontmatter field, no
title, no tag, no `_schema.yaml`, no page retired, no contradiction resolved. `git diff --stat` over
`wiki/proposals/` reads **27 files changed, 27 insertions, 1 deletion**, and the deletion is the
`status: current` the one `idea` page replaced. The field sits immediately after `sources:`, which
is where [[a-verdict-pairing-the-idea-status-with-a-named-decision]] already carried it and where
the `wiki/rules/` back-fill of 2026-08-23 put it.

**The method was the owner's of 2026-08-24 and it was not swept**
([[the-decided-by-back-fill-is-read-off-each-page-and-never-swept]]). Each page's own `sources:`
was opened, the journal named there was read — its `Decisions` and `Deferred` sections, and its
`Feedback to the librarian` where the cause lived only there — and then the `decisions/` page
compiled from that journal. Every one of the twenty-six targets was checked to be `type: decision`
before it was written. The report the owner ruled on named two candidate causes on seven of the
pages; **he ruled they change nothing today and are not to be re-opened**, so each was written as
the report proposed.

### The shape the deferral pages gave the answer

**Sixteen of the twenty-six point at a `binding: deferral` page and ten at a `binding: prohibition`
one**, and the split is not an accident of reading: this store files *that we said not now* as a
decision and *what we would build* as a proposal, so the aggregate deferral pages name their
proposals in the row that defers them. Four came out of
[[what-the-harness-build-waits-on]], four out of [[the-audits-findings-are-owed-to-the-owner]] and
three out of [[structure-work-agreed-and-not-executed]] — eleven of twenty-six from three pages,
each naming its proposal by wikilink in the table cell that prices the wait.

**Ten pages state their own cause in prose and were taken from their own words**, in the idiom the
rules back-fill also found: *"[[the-harness-is-compiled-not-maintained]] is the decision. This is
the design it would take"*; *"The decision is [[the-command-list-moves-into-a-makefile]]"*;
*"[[the-style-rule-is-ratified-and-its-text-recovered-from-the-approved-plan]] is the decision
behind it"*.

**One page had already written its cause into `sources:`**, which is the losing alternative
[[decided-by-is-a-field-of-its-own-and-not-a-line-in-sources]] rejected:
`wiki/proposals/migrating-the-repository-to-english.md` line 9 carries
`"[[english-is-the-rule-and-the-russian-past-is-deferred]]"` as a `sources:` entry. **That entry was
not removed** — nothing is deleted here — and the same page now names the same decision in the field
built for it. The duplicate is reported rather than repaired.

### One target is deprecated and lives in `archive/`, and it was written on the owner's instruction

**[[the-system-naming-which-hooks-block]] names [[advisory-is-the-default-for-a-hook]]**, which is
`type: decision`, `binding: prohibition`, `status: deprecated`, and sits at
`archive/2026-08-22/2026-08-22-the-strike-lands-and-a-quote-gets-a-verdict/pages/`. It is the cause:
lines 50-58 of that page quote the owner's «нужно будет обсудить что блокирует а что нет. Запишем на
будущее» of 2026-08-19 and close *"The design sits in [[the-system-naming-which-hooks-block]]"*. Its
live successor [[a-hook-refuses-on-a-measured-condition-a-reliable-measurement-and-a-refusal-that-says-how-to-clear-it]]
carries the same `binding:`, and says at its own line 118 that this proposal's retirement is the
owner's. **Rule 5c admits an archived target and the owner kept the case deliberately**, so the
deprecated page is what the field names.

### Six pages were left with no field, and the absence is the record

**`decided_by:` is optional in `wiki/proposals/` and the owner ruled an absent field better than a
false one.** These six each have a ruling in a journal and **no `decisions/` page compiled from
it**, so there is no legal target to name — the field would have to point at nothing, or `idea`
would have to assert *nobody decided this*, which the method forbids:

- [[a-machine-readable-format-for-the-registers]] — «Запиши, обсудим на следующей сессии»,
  `raw/handoffs/2026-08-21-a-claim-is-looked-up-before-a-page-is-written.md:233`;
- [[a-rule-usage-axis-for-vault-lint]] — «Это предложение сейчас не делаем»,
  `raw/handoffs/2026-08-20-the-pre-task-ritual-gets-a-moment-and-an-artefact.md:340-343`;
- [[lessons-become-a-queue-drained-into-proposals]] — the owner's design, deferred, same journal
  line 227;
- [[the-reading-funnel-is-delivered-as-a-procedure]] — deferred at the retro, same journal line 223;
- [[the-obsidian-cli-as-a-reading-surface-for-this-store]] — «да, запиши как proposal»,
  `archive/2026-08-23/2026-08-23-the-cause-of-a-page-becomes-a-field-and-the-style-rule-lands/handoffs/2026-08-23-the-cause-of-a-page-becomes-a-field-and-the-style-rule-lands.md:249`;
- [[the-suite-gets-a-scanner-exclusion-before-a-narrowed-gate]] — the owner ordered its second step
  on 2026-08-24, «стоит все таки уменьшить время его работы», recorded in `sprint.md` under
  `### Changes to the goal`, and the session executed it.

**Four of the six are one session's deferrals.** `raw/handoffs/2026-08-21-a-claim-is-looked-up-before-a-page-is-written.md`
has seven items in its `Deferred` section and **exactly one decision page was ever compiled from
it**, [[the-pre-task-enumeration-covers-every-folder-but-lessons]]. The proposals were written; the
deferrals behind them were not. **Six decision pages are owed and none was written here** — writing
them is compiling a journal, which is an ingest's act and not this run's.

### The one `status: idea`, and the one that was not

**[[telling-an-unfilled-retro-from-a-written-one]] took `status: idea`**, the first page in this
corpus ever to carry the value ([[an-idea-is-a-proposal-with-an-immature-status]]). It qualifies on
the record rather than on the search being hard: the session that raised it on 2026-08-19 wrote
*"Recorded rather than fixed, because `/retro` is a skill and its wording is not this session's to
change"* (`raw/handoffs/2026-08-19-the-gate-checked-itself-against-a-decoy-and-the-guard-objection-fell.md:455-465`),
and it was never put to the owner at all.

**[[the-suite-gets-a-scanner-exclusion-before-a-narrowed-gate]] was proposed as the second `idea`
and the owner refused that.** The verdict was right on the record read and stale against the day:
its second step was ordered on 2026-08-24 and executed this session, so it is not a half-thought
nobody ruled on. It joins the empty six instead. **A verdict read off a corpus can be correct and
already false**, which is the same shape as a brief that looks fresh when it is stale
([[the-brief-is-stamped-with-its-commit]]).

### `a-style-rule-for-the-prose-a-session-writes` got its field and not its placement

**It carries `status: implemented` and stays in `wiki/proposals/`.**
[[an-implemented-proposal-moves-to-archive-and-the-successor-carries-its-claim]] and
`wiki/proposals/_schema.yaml` both say such a page moves to `archive/`, and it has not. **The owner
ruled the disagreement real, recorded here rather than fixed, and the move a job for a script at the
lint stage that does not exist yet.** Nothing about the page's placement was touched.

- measure: **`git check-ignore --stdin` does not receive standard input under Windows PowerShell
  5.1.** In a fresh repository whose `.gitignore` holds `.superpowers/`, the argument form exits `0`
  and prints the path; the same paths piped to `--stdin` exit `1` and print nothing. `1` is also the
  honest *no path was ignored*, so the exit code cannot tell an empty answer from an empty input.
  **It fails towards nothing-is-ignored**, which in the handoff gate would refuse `/handoff` for
  ever. **Caught by a selftest case, not by review**

### The admission lookups, and where a new page was still right

- lookup: `--near check-system-arrangement` returned *already in group 'the selftest of the vault's
  own scripts'*. **That family holds the DECISIONS about the check system and no record of what was
  built**, so `the-makefile` was written as an `entities/` page and `makefile-targets` joined the same
  family. The proposal keeps the arrangement; the entity keeps what is on disk
- lookup: the hook family was read whole. `session-hooks` is the register and took three rows;
  `the-journal-gate-hook`, `the-plan-check-hook` and `the-pre-task-ledger` each own a different
  question. **None of them could carry *what the smoke gate is*, so one entity page covers the three
  hooks** rather than three pages for one mechanism's three halves
- lookup: `smoke-gate-inference` and `observed-run-verdict-source` were checked against
  `ledger-column-honesty` and `gate-delegation-reading`. The first owns what a ledger column may
  claim; the second owns the gate running the writer it checks. **Neither says where a verdict comes
  from when the hook did not run the command**, which is what the marker page is about
- lookup: `estimate-reasoning-error` against *a number this project quotes*. `claim-before-measurement`
  owns a claim made ahead of its measurement and `unrepeated-measurement` owns a single reading.
  **Neither says an estimate can be wrong in its model rather than its arithmetic**, which is the
  claim with the consequence — it is what makes people believe narrowing the suite cannot help
- lookup: `page-provenance-signature` against *a copy of a list drifts*. It is the same argument the
  family exists for, applied to a signature rather than a list, and the page joined that family
- lookup: `bulk-operation-ruling-check` and `archiver-runner-divergence`. **Both claims were already
  recorded inside other pages' dated sections** — the first on the CRLF ruling, the second nowhere.
  Written as `DIVERGENCE:` pages because that is the shape this corpus files a divergence in, and
  because the general claim in each is not about the page it was hiding in: *a bulk operation
  dissolves the moment a rule would be consulted*, and *a plan that divides an interleaved sequence
  between two parties is wrong at planning time*

- harness: /pre-task поймал три вещи, которые план не знал - что make style в vault-коммите не читает ничего, что коммит чужого ingest несёт пять команд ревью из ingest/SKILL.md, и что make smoke идёт дважды за сессию, а не раз. Ритуал окупился на плане, который выглядел проверенным.
- harness: фронтир, не взятый сегодня и подлежащий записи в спринт. Первое - субагент по решениям, читающий, с тремя входами: 120 прозаических упоминаний, 269 необработанных решений, 424 ссылки в отменённое. Второе - субагент по урокам, читающий, пишет черновик proposal в docs. Третье - перепроводка ingest под схему, где диспатчит сессия, а не библиотекарь. Четвёртое - впускная сторона, с зацепкой: сегодняшний ingest дал 10 новых страниц против 24 датированных секций на существующих, и долю "могло быть секцией" никто не мерил. Пятое - entities и concepts, 169 страниц без критерия выхода, отложены сегодня явно. Шестое - выход агента по решениям не оценён, и первый прогон и есть измерение: коридор "останется между 150 и 269" это цена того, что его не мерили.
- harness: одно требование про VAULT-FEEDBACK теперь написано в двух файлах хуков для двух ритуалов - в голове remind-the-smoke.ps1 для /retro и целиком в remind-the-feedback.ps1 для каждого промпта. Убирает дублирование один хук, владеющий требованием и называющий ритуалы, и это правка обоих файлов, а не добавление к одному.
- harness: форма строки вычёркивания в sprint.md шире правила, которое ею управляет - она называет и страницу ответа, и артефакт в дереве, а an-answered-item-leaves-the-next-list-by-being-struck-in-place требует страницу. Двадцать три строки уже написаны в этой форме, и следующий, кто будет вычёркивать, скопирует их, а не правило. Нужно либо ратифицировать расширение, либо сузить строки.
- harness: --only у scripts/vault-check-selftest.sh нужно починить или задокументировать как дефект. Сегодня это подстрочный glob, шаблон с вертикальными чертами не совпадает ни с чем, а inline-кейсы фильтр не проходят вовсе - поэтому пустой прогон печатает caught 1, missed 0 - FILTERED и читается как успешная проверка.
- harness: точка MessageDisplay зарегистрирована и срабатывает на каждый ответ ассистента. Именно там жил бы счётчик ходов с последнего блока, покрывающий сессию, которая замолкает в собственных ответах. UserPromptSubmit покрывает рулинги владельца и этого не покрывает.
